entities.summary: Charles Montagu, 1st Duke of Manchester, was a British aristocrat and statesman who played a crucial role in shaping the country's politics during the early 18th century. He was born in 1670 and died in 1722. Montagu served as the Chancellor of the Exchequer and was a key figure in the development of the Bank of England. He also played a significant role in the Jacobite rising of 1715, which aimed to restore the Stuart dynasty to the British throne. Montagu's legacy can be seen in the establishment of the Manchester Townshend Charter, which granted local self-government to the town of Manchester. This innovation had a lasting impact on the development of democratic institutions in the region. Montagu's contributions to the Bank of England and the Manchester Townshend Charter demonstrate his commitment to the advancement of commerce and the welfare of his constituents. His statesmanship and leadership helped to shape the course of British history, making him a significant figure in the annals of early modern history.
